Resolves #17816

Card-layout children now release Flexbox's automatic minimum size on both direct and transition-wrapper render paths. A Grid or TreeGrid therefore remains constrained to its Card viewport when resized columns become wider, allowing the existing horizontal scrollbar to own the overflow. Explicit component minimum sizes remain authoritative.

Evidence: L3 (real Chromium Card/Grid/TreeGrid resize and scrollbar reachability) → L3 required (all close-target runtime ACs). No residuals.

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge — the regression surface is covered by specs this PR cannot run.**

The change alters min-size behavior for **every direct child of every Card layout**, and `src/tab/Container.mjs` gives its `BodyContainer` a card layout — so every tab container in the repository inherits it. That is the correct scope for the fix and it is also a wide silent-change surface: anything that relied on the implicit `min-width: auto` floor now shrinks.

Where would that show? I enumerated it: **six** e2e specs touch tab or card, including `WorkstationResidentCardSizingNL.spec.mjs` — named for exactly this behavior — plus `LockedCellHorizontalStability`, `DockTabOverflowNL`, `WorkstationTabOverflowCapNL`. **None of them ran here.** The classifier emits only `run_unit` and `run_components`; there is no e2e job in the PR check surface at all, and its whitelist correctly routes live-compiled theme SCSS to components. **The classifier did the right thing — the coverage simply lives on the other side of the gate.**

So "components pass" is true and narrow: of 19 component specs, exactly one exercises Card children, and it is this PR's own. Not a false green — the new spec is thorough for its scenarios — but the question *did any existing Card child change size* has no instrument on this PR.

I am not treating that as blocking, for three reasons: the identical release already ships one flex boundary higher (`DockLayoutAdapter.mjs:790-794`, with a comment naming the same mechanism) without incident; the explicit-minimum escape hatch is tested here at two layers; and releasing `min-width: auto` is the standard remedy — a child wanting a floor should declare one. Cheapest coverage would be running those four e2e specs locally once, or naming them as post-merge validation.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: The spec is a model for browser regression tests. It asserts the **pre-state** (`expect(before.scrollRange, 'fixed columns begin narrower than the viewport').toBe(0)`) so the post-state means something; it puts a **positive control on its own action** (`'resize must engage (before=…, after=…)'`) before measuring the effect; it asserts the **mechanism** (`after.minWidth === '0px'`) and the **user-visible outcome** (`'the final column is reachable at max scroll'`) separately; and it covers both Grid and TreeGrid because the ticket says both are affected. A test that cannot distinguish "the fix worked" from "the action never happened" is the common failure here, and this one cannot make that mistake.
